name: vm-manager
description: Manage virtual machines (Hyper-V, QEMU, Proxmox, ...) from VS Code: clusters, nodes, power actions, graphical and serial consoles.

scripts.build: npm run build:webview && npm run build:extension

viewsWelcome.contents:
No hypervisor provider is installed yet. Providers are separate extensions so each hypervisor can be updated independently.
[$(extensions) Install a Provider](command:vmm.installProviders)
[Get Started](command:vmm.showWalkthrough)

No clusters configured. A cluster groups the nodes (hosts) of one hypervisor, for example your local Hyper-V or a Proxmox cluster.
[$(add) Add Cluster](command:vmm.addCluster)
[Get Started](command:vmm.showWalkthrough)

No groups yet. Make one, then add machines with Add to Group… on a machine, or drag them here from Clusters.
[$(new-folder) New Group](command:vmm.newGroup)

vmm.refreshInterval.markdownDescription: Seconds between state refreshes while the Clusters view or the Overview is visible. Providers that push change events refresh immediately.

vmm.console.openInNewWindow.description: Open consoles directly in a new window instead of an editor tab.

vmm.console.scaleViewport.description: Scale graphical consoles to fit the editor.

vmm.confirmPowerOff.description: Ask for confirmation before a hard power off (Stop).

vmm.ssh.user.markdownDescription: The account to sign in as inside a guest when connecting with **VM: Connect with Remote-SSH…**. Empty: your user name on this computer. The answer is remembered per machine.

vmm.ssh.addConfigEntry.markdownDescription: Offer to add an entry for the machine to your ssh config before connecting (it is always shown first and never written silently). Turn off to connect by address without touching the file.

enumDescriptions: Only changes VS Code did not ask for: a guest that shut itself down, a machine started or stopped in another tool, a crash.
Every change, also the ones you asked for here.
No notifications; changes are still written to each machine's log (VM: Show Log).
vmm.notifications.stateChanges.markdownDescription: Tell you when a virtual machine starts, stops, pauses or resumes. Changes are noticed while VM Manager refreshes: when the Virtual Machines view or the Overview is visible, or when the provider reports them (QEMU does).

enumDescriptions: Your groups (VM: Add to Group…); a machine in two groups is in both, the rest under Not in a group.
vmm.tree.groupBy.markdownDescription: How the Clusters view groups machines. Favorites and your groups also have their own view below it.

vmm.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Run an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server so AI agents outside VS Code (Claude Code, other MCP clients) can list and drive your machines. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, needs an access token (**VM: Copy MCP Server Setup**), and asks you before every action.

vmm.mcp.port.markdownDescription: Port of the MCP server on 127.0.0.1 (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`).

vmm.agent.allowDestructive.markdownDescription: Let AI agents (agent mode in VS Code and MCP clients) power off or reset machines and revert or delete snapshots. Each call is still confirmed. Off: those calls are refused.

vmm.qemu.path.markdownDescription: Directory containing `qemu-system-*` and `qemu-img`. Leave empty to detect from `PATH` and common install locations. Clusters can override this.

vmm.proxmox.rememberSession.markdownDescription: Keep the Proxmox sign-in (OpenID Connect or password) in the operating system keychain after VS Code closes or reloads, so the next start reuses it while it is valid (Proxmox sessions last 2 hours) instead of asking again. Off: the session is forgotten when VS Code closes. **Sign Out** always removes it.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with VM Manager
walkthroughs.description: Manage Hyper-V, QEMU and other hypervisors without leaving VS Code.

steps.title: Install a hypervisor provider
steps.description:
Each hypervisor is supported by its own small extension, so it can be updated independently.
[Install Providers](command:vmm.installProviders)

steps.title: Add your first cluster
steps.description:
A cluster is one hypervisor installation, for example ``Local (Hyper-V)``. It contains nodes (hosts) which run your virtual machines.
[Add Cluster](command:vmm.addCluster)

media.altText: Cluster, node and virtual machine hierarchy

steps.title: Create or pick a virtual machine
steps.description:
Right-click a node to create a virtual machine, or use the actions next to an existing one to start, shut down, reboot or stop it.
[Create Virtual Machine](command:vmm.createVm)

steps.title: Connect to a console
steps.description:
Graphical consoles use noVNC and serial consoles use xterm, right inside an editor tab. Use **Open in New Window** in the editor toolbar to pop a console out.
[Connect Graphical Console](command:vmm.connectGraphical)

steps.title: See everything at a glance
steps.description:
The overview shows every cluster, node and virtual machine with its state and resources.
[Open Overview](command:vmm.openOverview)

steps.title: Your credentials stay safe
steps.description: Passwords and API tokens are stored in the operating system keychain through VS Code Secret Storage. They are never written to settings files and never sent to the webviews.

vm.description: The machine: its name, cluster/name when two clusters have one of that name, or an id from the VM Manager API.

action.description: What to do. start does nothing on a running machine, shutdown and stop nothing on one that is off.

enumDescriptions: Until the machine is running (start, reboot, reset) or off (shutdown, stop).
Also until it has an IP address.
Also until an SSH server answers (a port forward to 22, or its address).
Not at all once the hypervisor accepted the action.
waitFor.description: What the task waits for before it ends.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait in all before the task fails.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_list_clusters
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the hypervisor clusters configured in VM Manager (local QEMU, libvirt, Hyper-V, Proxmox, Nutanix…), whether they are connected, and their nodes with the number of machines on each.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_list_vms
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the virtual machines and containers of every cluster with their state, IP addresses, vCPUs and memory. Filter by state, cluster or a text in the name. Use this first to find the machine to work on.

cluster.description: Only machines of the cluster with this name.

name.description: Only machines whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

languageModelTools.name: vmm_get_vm
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Describes one machine: state, addresses, its disks, network adapters (with MAC and IP addresses), port forwards and devices, and what can be done with it here (power actions, snapshots, commands in the guest, file copies).

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_get_vm_stats
languageModelTools.modelDescription: One sample of a running machine's usage: CPU (0..1), memory used and total in MB, uptime, and cumulative disk and network byte counters (take two samples to compute a rate).

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_list_snapshots
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the snapshots of a machine, oldest first, with their id, name, time and whether they hold memory state.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_get_vm_address
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Where to reach a running machine: an IP address, or with ssh=true a host and port where an SSH server answers (a port forward for machines behind NAT). Can wait for the machine to come up.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

ssh.description: Return an address where SSH answers (checked with a banner probe) instead of any IP address.

waitSeconds.description: Keep trying this long while there is no address yet (0 to 600).

languageModelTools.name: vmm_power_vm
languageModelTools.displayName: Start, shut down or restart a virtual machine
languageModelTools.userDescription: Start, shut down or restart a virtual machine
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Changes a machine's power state. start, shutdown (asks the guest to shut down) and reboot are ordinary actions; stop (immediate power off) and reset (hard reset) lose unsaved guest data and are only allowed when the user enabled destructive actions. With wait=true it returns once the machine reached the new state.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

wait.description: Wait until the machine is running (start, reboot, reset) or stopped (shutdown, stop).

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait at most (default 120, at most 600).

languageModelTools.name: vmm_wait_for_state
languageModelTools.displayName: Wait for a virtual machine state
languageModelTools.userDescription: Wait for a virtual machine state
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Waits until a machine reaches a state (for example running after a start that was not waited for) and returns it.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

waitSeconds.description: At most this long (default 120, at most 600).

languageModelTools.name: vmm_take_snapshot
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Saves the current state of a machine as a named snapshot it can be reverted to later. Take one before risky changes inside the guest.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_revert_snapshot
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a machine to a snapshot, discarding everything changed since. Destructive: only allowed when the user enabled destructive actions.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

snapshot.description: The snapshot id or name from vmm_list_snapshots.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_delete_snapshot
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Deletes a snapshot of a machine. Destructive: only allowed when the user enabled destructive actions.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

snapshot.description: The snapshot id or name from vmm_list_snapshots.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_run_in_guest
languageModelTools.displayName: Run a command in a virtual machine
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run a command in a virtual machine
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs a program inside a running machine through its guest agent (qemu-guest-agent) and returns its exit code, stdout and stderr. Use shell=true for a command line with pipes or variables (/bin/sh -c, or cmd.exe /c on Windows). Each call is confirmed by the user.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

command.description: The program (absolute path is safest), or with shell=true the whole command line.

shell.description: Run command through the guest's shell.

input.description: Text given to the program on stdin.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for it (default 60, at most 600). It keeps running in the guest after a timeout.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_copy_to_guest
languageModelTools.displayName: Copy a file into a virtual machine
languageModelTools.userDescription: Copy a file into a virtual machine
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Copies a file from this computer into a running machine through its guest agent, replacing the file at guestPath. Each call is confirmed by the user.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

localPath.description: Absolute path of the file on this computer.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_copy_from_guest
languageModelTools.displayName: Copy a file out of a virtual machine
languageModelTools.userDescription: Copy a file out of a virtual machine
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Copies a file from a running machine to this computer through its guest agent, replacing the file at localPath. Each call is confirmed by the user.

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.

languageModelTools.name: vmm_add_port_forward
languageModelTools.displayName: Forward a port to a virtual machine
languageModelTools.userDescription: Forward a port to a virtual machine
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Forwards a port on this computer (localhost) to a port in a machine behind NAT, for example host 2222 to guest 22 for SSH. Only for providers with port forwarding (QEMU, local libvirt).

vm.description: The machine: its name, "cluster/name" when names repeat across clusters, or its id from vmm_list_vms.
